div.h2: Project budgets built from the bill of quantities
div.p: A construction budget starts with the BOQ. In Odoo you set up each project with its phases, work packages and BOQ lines, and the planned quantity and cost of every line become the budget that actual spending is measured against. Your estimators keep working in Excel if they prefer, and we import the BOQ into the project instead of asking anyone to retype it.

The project manager then sees budget against committed cost and actual cost for the whole project or for a single phase, so an overrun shows up while there is still time to act on it instead of at final account.

Every purchase order, vendor bill, timesheet, stock issue and expense can carry a project and a cost code through analytic accounting. Because the tagging happens on the transaction itself, job costing is a by-product of normal work and not a month-end spreadsheet exercise.

Finance can then report profit and loss by project, by phase or by cost code, and compare the result with the original estimate. The same data feeds the company ledger, so the project figures and the accounts always agree.

Subcontract work is managed against an agreed scope and value. Each interim payment starts as a progress certificate that records the work completed to date, deducts what was certified before, applies any retention percentage and produces the amount due. Approvals follow the sequence you define, from site engineer to quantity surveyor to finance.
Because the certificate becomes the vendor bill, the subcontractor ledger, the retention balance and the project cost are all updated from one document.

div.h2: Variation orders, progress billing and retention
div.p: Variation orders are recorded as changes to the contract value and the budget, with their own approval trail, so scope changes are not lost in email. Client invoices are raised as progress claims against the contract, either by percentage complete or by BOQ item measured on site.
Retention held back by the client is tracked as a separate receivable with its own release conditions, so finance knows how much is locked up on each project and when it is due.

div.h2: From material requisition to vendor bill
div.p: Site teams raise a material requisition against a project. Purchasing turns it into requests for quotation, compares vendor prices, and issues the purchase order after the approvals your policy requires. The goods are received into a site store, and the vendor bill is matched against the order and the receipt before it is paid.
Materials can be transferred between sites and the central warehouse, and each issue to site is charged to the right project and cost code.

div.h2: Site labour, timesheets and UAE payroll
div.p: Labour is often the largest cost on site. Daily or weekly timesheets record hours by worker, project and activity, and the cost flows to the job automatically. Overtime, camp and transport allowances and deductions follow the rules you configure.

Payroll runs from the same employee records and can prepare salary files in the WPS format that UAE banks expect. Contract, visa and ID expiry dates are kept on the employee file so renewals are not missed.

p.a: See HR and payroll software for UAE companies

div.p: Cranes, generators, vehicles and tools are registered as assets and assigned to projects, with maintenance schedules, running costs and depreciation tracked per item. Fleet records keep insurance and registration renewals visible.

Drawings, contracts, permits, submittals and correspondence are stored against the project with version history and access rights, so the site team and the head office work from the same current documents.

div.h2: VAT on progress invoices and multi-company groups
div.p: Progress invoices, retention releases and subcontractor bills carry the correct UAE VAT treatment, and the VAT return is prepared from the same ledger entries. Corporate Tax records and the move toward structured e-invoicing are handled in the same accounting setup.

Contractors that operate several legal entities, for example a main contractor, a trading arm and a joint venture, can run them as separate companies in one database with consolidated reporting and inter-company transactions.

div.p: Front-desk staff register a patient once and reuse the record for every visit, with contact details, identification and the payer on file. Appointments are booked against a doctor, a room or a service, and reminders can be sent by email or message so fewer slots go unused.
Online booking can be offered on your website, with the calendar showing only the times that are genuinely free for each doctor.

A visit moves from check-in to consultation, procedures, prescriptions and checkout, and each step is visible to the next person in the chain. Services and packages are priced in a price list, so what the doctor orders is exactly what billing charges.
Clinical record needs differ by specialty, so we confirm in discovery what must be captured in the system and what stays in your existing medical software, and we scope the setup around that.

Medicines and consumables are tracked by lot with an expiry date, so the oldest stock is used first and items close to expiry are flagged before they become waste. Reordering rules raise a purchase request when a product falls below the level you set for a location.
Stock can be held in the pharmacy, the clinic rooms and a central store, with transfers recorded between them and a full movement history for audit.

Invoices can be split between the patient and the insurer according to the policy, with co-payment and deductible handled as separate lines. Self-pay, corporate and insurance patients each follow their own billing path.

Claims are tracked from submission through to payment and rejection, so finance can follow up outstanding amounts by insurer. Any exchange of claim data with external platforms is scoped with you during discovery, because requirements vary by facility.

Because the lead, the appointment and the invoice live in one system, you can see which campaigns bring patients who actually attend, not just clicks.

div.h2: UAE VAT on every POS receipt
div.p: Retail in the UAE means a high volume of small VAT transactions. In Odoo, each product carries its tax setting, so every POS receipt shows the VAT amount per line and the order total, whether prices are entered tax-inclusive or tax-exclusive. Odoo's UAE localization provides the standard 5% rate together with zero-rated and exempt treatments, and every sale posts to the ledger automatically when the session is closed.
That means the figures your accountant reviews come from the same transactions the cashier rang up. There is no re-keying from till reports into a spreadsheet.

p.a: See how this connects to the rest of the books: accounting software for the UAE

div.p: The UAE is moving businesses to structured electronic invoicing through accredited service providers, on a phased timeline set by the Ministry of Finance and the Federal Tax Authority. For a retailer, the practical work is clean master data: correct tax registration numbers, consistent product and tax codes, and customer records that can be validated.

Techrise reviews your setup against current guidance, cleans the data that invoices depend on, and plans the integration with you so you are not scrambling when your turn comes. Requirements differ by business size and sales type, so we confirm the details with you during discovery instead of promising a one-size-fits-all switch.

Every store, warehouse and stockroom is a location in Odoo Inventory. You see on-hand quantities per branch and in total, move goods between stores with transfer orders, and receive supplier deliveries against purchase orders. Reordering rules raise a replenishment request when a product drops below the minimum you set for a location.
Barcode scanning speeds up receiving, stocktakes and picking, and lot or serial numbers cover products that need traceability.

div.h2: A POS that keeps selling offline
div.p: Odoo POS runs in the browser on a tablet, a PC or a touch terminal. After a session is opened, the till can continue to take orders if the internet connection drops, and the orders sync to the server once the connection returns. Queues at the counter do not depend on your network provider.

Cashiers work with product search, barcode scanning, discounts, split payments and customer lookup. Managers open and close shifts, count cash and review a session report. Receipts and product names can be maintained in Arabic and English, and the interface supports right-to-left display.

div.h2: Loyalty programs, gift cards and promotions
div.p: Loyalty points, discount rules, coupons and gift cards are configured once and work at the till and on your online store. You can reward repeat customers, run a time-limited promotion on a product category, or sell gift cards that are redeemed in any branch.

Because every sale is tied to a customer record, you also get purchase history in the same place your team keeps contact details. That makes targeted offers possible without exporting data to a separate marketing tool.

Odoo Website and eCommerce share the product catalog and stock with your stores. An item sold online reduces the same stock count a cashier sees, so you avoid selling what you no longer have. Online orders flow into delivery and invoicing the same way store sales do.
Marketplace and social channels can be connected through integrations that we scope with you. We tell you plainly what is available as standard and what needs custom work before you commit.

div.h2: Reporting that shows what is selling
div.p: Sales, margin and stock reports can be filtered by branch, product category, cashier or period. Owners see which items sell fast and which sit on the shelf, finance sees profit and loss across all channels together, and store managers see their own numbers without waiting for head office.
